notes: The two מִן phrases are rendered in the reverse of the Hebrew order: the ablative on the verb becomes for us at the end of the clause and the privative keeps the written infinitive marker, so both units are reordered under rule 25.
The privative מִן takes the written to as the function word the recasting spends on it, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied infinitive marker does (rules 48, 52).
